items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019

ctx.x: to play if you loved swing music and loved big band music, the only way to play it in 1979 or ’80 for a young musician was in these kind of like second rate bands that played stock arrangements or transcriptions and you might have three or four really great players in the band and some others that weren’t so great. It was a lot of fun and it paid. But it was not at all excellent playing. So one of those bands was a band led by a guy named Bob January. And the singer in his band was Barbara Lea. And we became…

players and — it was about fifty percent young and fifty percent older, of course much — the old guys were younger than I am now. And so the band started to cotton. And in the meantime Goodman asked me to come back because this woman I had mentioned before, Muriel Zuckerman, who had been his Girl Friday, she quit, and he said, “Can you come in and just, until I find someone, answer the phones or just help with something?” So I started doing that, and then eventually when he found out that I knew musicians and I…

Later on, as the band got professional and as I started to make a living in music, all those guys, I mean I paid. I paid for arrangements. I paid arrangers and I paid — but at this time there was nothing there. So John Hammond and a few other things and things started, and next thing you know we’re going to make a record. So we made a record for a guy named Jerry Valburn who issued a lot of radio broadcasts with like a big jazz collector who had his own little labels. And he had a label and he started recording…
